title: The Apple I's $666.66 price
hook: Apple's first computer cost $666.66 because Wozniak liked repeating digits.
peek: In 1976 the Apple I went on sale for $666.66. The number had nothing to do with omens: Steve Wozniak simply liked how repeating digits looked, and the sum was a tidy markup on the dealer price.
lede: In July 1976 a small company called Apple started selling its first computer, the Apple I, for $666.66. Steve Wozniak, who designed it, later explained the odd figure: he liked numbers with repeating digits, and it was roughly a one-third markup on the $500 a shop paid for each board. He said he had no idea anyone would read anything darker into it.

bullets.text: Paul Terrell, who ran the Byte Shop in Mountain View, California, ordered 50 machines at $500 each. That order turned Apple from a hobby into a business, and set the price the retail figure was built on.

bullets.opening: Selling a van and a calculator
bullets.text: To pay for parts, Steve Jobs sold his Volkswagen van and Wozniak sold his HP-65 programmable calculator. The two founders raised about $1,300 between them.
Buyers got a fully assembled circuit board and little else. They had to add their own keyboard, power supply, display and usually a wooden case. Only about 200 were made.
Surviving working boards now sell at auction for hundreds of thousands of dollars, many hundreds of times the original $666.66.
